correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact three-class generator directly from each ordered-pair transition. Backward equations give three rational Laplace transforms normalized by Delta(0)=4 alpha beta kappa. Positive symmetrizability plus middle-state killing give real, positive, simple poles; secular interlacing locates them relative to 2 alpha and 2 beta. Signed pole residues prove h_D strictly decreasing, h_A/h_B increasing from slower parts, and a unique maximum from the faster part because its derivative-sign factor strictly decreases from positive to negative. Equal-rate cancellation preserves strict monotonicity. Direct full ordered-pair rational generator test passed 426 identities; spectral samples passed 18 classifications. Finite tests do not replace the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The reviewed general meeting-time transform framework of Ohwa is broader in method but does not evaluate location-dependent class rates on arbitrary complete bipartite graphs or the all-parameter unimodal-versus-monotone encounter-hazard threshold. Discrete-time regular-graph mean results and end-absorbing birth–death hazard results do not imply the three-state middle-absorbing sign classification. A prior homogeneous-rate equal-part statement does not contain the faster-part unique-maximum regime. Five targeted claim/alias searches and additional related-parameter searches in the searchable published finding index returned no equivalent claim. This is originality relative to inspected material, not an exhaustive priority guarantee.

value.rationale: The natural first-encounter hazard contains kinetic information absent from mean or limiting decay rates. The theorem completely classifies three initial-placement geometries and finds an exact speed-order boundary for a unique nonmonotone encounter-hazard peak, independent of two graph sizes. This separates effects of mobility and network topology for a fundamental two-particle collision observable; it is not simply substituting parameters in an existing evaluated homogeneous-rate formula.
